F.I.R. Contents (Attached complaint report)
On 11.10.2023 at 12.00 hrs received an English typed report from Shri D.
Vasudeva Reddy, Commissioner of Distilleries & Breweries, and Managing
Director, Andhra Pradesh State BeveragesCorporation Ltd.,O/C Commissioner of
Prohibitionand Excise,Survey No. 88-2B,Sai Vihar Apartments, Prasadampadu
Vijayawada-52110 Stating the following:
The Corporation, as an entity created under the Statute with monopoly over the subject
activity, undertook a periodic review of the policies of the State in the past, in pursuance
of the stated policy of the State for progressive prohibition. The Corporation has been
working in consonance with the policy decisions of the State since 2015. While
undertaking a review of the earnings and revenue for the State at the relevant point in
time during 2014-2019, the following glaring policy decisions came to light, which had
the effect of reducing the revenues for the State and benefitting the licencees. It was also
found out that contrary to the recommendations of the Committee constituted for the
purpose by the Government of AP, few distilleries were favoured by giving LOl: New
brands were permitted by the public servants, after notification Dt. 18.03.2019 for
general election was issued, without there being any public interest therefor. It is also
startling that the suppliers, in conspiracy and collusion with the licencees, exaggerated
the demand for certain products, without there being a market demand for the same,
thereby resulting in distorted projection being given to the Corporation. There being no
mechanism for verification of the actual demand, the data of the supplies and the
quantities for the relevant period 2015-2019, shows that a few companies were preferred,
and orders were placed for their products disproportionate to their market share, to the
extent of 70% of the brands being garnered by identified individual suppliers. The
procurements undertaken, clearly discern that as a part of a prior concert, design, and
common intention, perhaps with the participation of various public servants at various
stages of decision making, were to confer unlawful pecuniary gain to a few entities. The
data sheet showing the quantities supplied by various entities is enclosed herewith,
which may need further investigation.
The detailed study of the decisions taken between 2014-2019 to help the Corporation
to recommend suitable policy changes for the future, clearly pointed out the following
specific instances of decisions resulting in loss of revenue to the Government, and
conferment of pecuniary gain to the licencees. In the draft performance report Principal
Accountant General (Audit) infraction resulted loss to the exchequer are noted and the is
in the public domain. A detailed enquiry/investigation is essential to unravel the
criminality in the decision-making process, criminal conspiracy, and intent to violate the
rules and orient the policy decisions to suit the pecuniary interests of the licencees.
1. Decision making in relation to the quantum and the decision not to flx Privilege
fee.
The statutory rules in regard to imposition of privilege fee on A4 Shop Licencees
was introduced in the year 2012 vide statutory rules in GO Ms. No. 391 dt. 16.6.2012.
The statutory rules in regard to imposition of privilege fee on A4 Shop Licencees was introduced in the year 2012 vide statutory rules in GO Ms. No. 391 dt. 16.6.2012. The privilege fce prescribed being 8% plus VAT on the turnover of purchases by the said அருள்மிகு ,

such imposition, the licencees resorted to disguised sales, accounting manipulations
regarding sale of stocks.
While initiating the decision making for the excise years 2015-2017, it was initially
proposed that the threshold limit for imposition of privilege fee be enhanced to be
applicable only if the purchases exceed ten times the annual licence feeso that there is
incentive for compliance with the statutory rules and compliance. This was to rationalize
the revenue collections and to motivate the licencees to abide by the statute and to
disincentivize the inclination to under-record and manipulate the record of sale by
licencees. However, the said initiative did not secure any further progress in the decision
making.
While forwarding the inputs for finalization of the policy for A4 shops, broadly which was
taken to the cabinet for finalization, only salient features of the excise policy as forwarded
was taken into account. The cabinet note laconically refers to the broad outline of the
decisions as salient features of the policy on 17.06.2015 primarily regarding the
methodology of allotment of shops by drawal of lots, running of 10% shops by the
Corporation and the new eligibility criteria to be fixed, as indicated in the series of
cabinet notes circulated for the above. Process was initiated on 22.06.2015 for
amendment of rules Licence Rules comprised in GO Ms. No. 391 dt. 18.6.2012 and on
the same day GOMs No.218 Revenue (Excise-II) was issued without any discussions
about any financial implication and in utter disregard to the procedure prescribed.
The proposal submitted for the amendment of statutory rules was moved on
22.6.2015, by CPE, in DO No CR No. 999/2015/CPE/E3 dt. 22.6.2015 which contained
the draft rules to be amended, including the deletion of Rule 16(9) of the Licence Rules,
2012, thereby removing the existing privilege fee on Shop Licencees. On the said
proposal, the statutory rules in GO Ms. No. 218 dt. 22.6.2015 is issued duly deleting
Rule 16(9) of the Licence Rules comprised in GO Ms. No. 391 dt. 18.6.2012. It is to be
seen that to secure such deletionof the privilege fee, contrary to the initial proposal to
continue the privilege fee, if the purchases cross 10 times the annual licence fee, the said
rule was notified removing the privilege fee altogether.
It is curious to note that the earnings of the Government on account of the
privilege fee between 2012-2015 is Rs.2984 Crores. (which includes the period in the
composite State of AP). Apparently, the loss of earnings to the Government is the
immediate consequence of the above decision, which under the Business Rules, requires
the said proposal, to be sent to the Finance Department for its clearance, under Rule
11(a)(ii) and15(1).of the Business Rules,2013 as applicable at the relevant time.
Furthermore, the decision to delete the privilege fee, did not form part of the excise policy
deliberations forwarded to the cabinet, as reflected in the record, an in-depth
investigation is required to unravel the nexus between the decision taken by the persons
who are at the helm of affairs and the stake holders during the relevant point of time. An
important decision relating to privilege fee was taken without reference to the cabinet
approval and the same did not form part of the salient features of the policy placed. It

In pursuance of the same, citing the said example, the similar proposal for deletion
of the imposition of privilege fee on the turnover of the 2B-Bars cropped up during the
year 2015. The existing Rules, as on the said date, ns contained in Rule 10(a) @ 9% on
the sale price of IMFL purchased from the Corporation, when the cumulative value
exceeds six times of the licence fee. Taking cue from the policy decision taken in 2015,
removing privilege fee for the A4 Shop licencees, a representation dt. 09.09.2015 is
received from the Association of AP State Wine Dealers, requesting for similar deletion of
privilege fee for bar licenccees also. Based on the same, while formulating the process for
the excise year 2016, to be made effective from 01.01.2016, the proposal to delete the
same even for bars, is initiated on 30.09.2015. It could be discernable that a separate
excise policy for Bars for 2015-2016 is mooted and subsequent discussions are shown to
have been held on 23.11.2015 with the then Honourable Chief Minister and then
Honourable Minister for Excise the outline of the new Bar Policy for 2016 is shown to
have been arrived. The proposal is composite one including the proposal to delete the
existing privilege fee for Bars, based on their turnover. The financial implications arising
from the said proposal are not discussed. The file is not circulated to the finance
department as required under the Business Rules. The proposed amendments removing
the obligation of privilege fee payable by Bars, as contained in Rule 10(a), is placed as
detailed above before the then Hon'ble Chief Minister and Excise Minister who approved
for such deletion of privilege fee without any procedural adherence and by circumventing
the basic mandatory requirements. A visible picture is emerging that distinct bar excise
policy for 2016, is a departure from the existing rules, contemplating removal of privilege
fee payable by Bars on turnover, is finalized by the then Chief Minister and the Excise
Minister, without reference to the cabinet, or the council of Ministers by limiting the
circulation of the file in the above manner.Thus, the matter needs to be investigated for
abuse of office by public servants, loss to the state exchequer, compromise to the public
interest, and the corresponding unlawful pecuniary gain to the licenccees. Therefore, a
decision of huge financial implications amounting to around Rs. 1300 crore, loss of
revenue to the State and corresponding benefit to the A4 shop owners as is noticeable in
explicitly in terms and a is clear abuse of office by the public servants, in compromise to
public interest, in an illegal process of circumventing and by passing the procedure
under Business Rules.

the public exchequer. Notwithstanding the said directions, further benefit of payment of
instalments was granted, interest on the arrears in licence fee was allowed to be collected
only w.e.f. 27.11.2015 (the date of judgement of the High Court in PIL No. 102/2015),
contrary to the findings of the judgement. The interest payable for the period prior
thereto, on the arrears of licence fee, was relaxed, by recourse to Section 65 of AP Excise

In fact, there is no provision under the Act and Rules to give up or indirectly waive the
interest payable or enforce from a future date (as opposed to the dates from which
interest is payable). More so when it is expressly contrary to the findings of the Hon'ble
High Court, which found fault with SPY for non -compliance with the statutory rules.
The financial loss caused to the Government and corresponding pecuniary gain to the
SPY on account of enforcement of interest only from 27.11.2015 and not from the earlier
date of accrual dues, amounts approximately @18% is fifteen (15) crores. A detailed
investigation is necessary, including into the possibility of quid pro quo having regard to
the fact that the promoter Sri SPY Reddy, is a politician and MP from Nandyal at the
relevant point in time.
3.Permission for grant of Distillery:
Contrary to the recommendations of the committee constituted under GO
Rt.No.993, Revenue (Excise-II) Department dt.12.11.2014, permission was granted to
establishment of Distilleries beyond the recommended capacity by the Committee. As per
the Rules governing the committee, the Government is bound by the recommendations of
the Committee and without reference to any further justification, factual or legal, such a
decision was taken, in a departure from rules, to benefit the private distilleries i.e., M/s
P.M.K Distilleries, M/s Visakha Distilleries and three others.
4. Undue favour to few suppliers/distilleries:
In conspiracy and collusion with the stakeholders an element of exaggeration in
creating a demand for certain products, without there being a market demand for the
same, thereby resulting in distorted projection being given to the Corporation. There
being no mechanism for verification of the actual demand, the data of the supplies and
the quantities for the relevant period 2015-2019, shows that four to five companies were
preferred on selective basis for extraneous reasons, and orders were placed for their
products to an extent of 70% of the brands being garnered by identified individual
suppliers. The procurements undertaken, clearly as a part of a prior concert, design, and
common intention, perhaps with the participation of various public servants at various
stages of decision making, were to confer unlawful pecuniary gain to a few entities. The
data sheet showing the quantities supplied to various entities is enclosed herewith,
which may need further investigation.
